import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<Aside type="caution" title="Partially built — model is being implemented in phases">
This page records the security model for **shared harnesses** (the peer-to-peer,
multi-engineer sync substrate), the research it rests on, and the tradeoffs we are
choosing **intentionally**. The model below is the agreed direction, tracked in the design
memo `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-trust-model-2026-05-31.md`. Sections marked
**Today** describe the original (2026-05-31) insecure state; **Recommended** describes the
target.

**Build-state update (2026-06-13).** The substrate trust layer is now substantially built:
**per-log admission** (signed announce + GitHub-anchored `verifyBinding` attestation),
**revocation** (`revoked_pubkeys` projection drop-list, gated on a live GitHub repo-admin
check), and **identity attestation** (`verifyAttestation`) are all wired. Crucially, a
confirmation audit (P-017, plan `shared-pot-hardening-2026-06-13`) verified that the
model's load-bearing invariant — **every decision-bearing fact re-derives from GitHub at
the point of action** — holds across all current call sites. See
[The advisory-vs-trusted boundary](#the-advisory-vs-trusted-boundary) for the verified
call-site table. Per-op signing (Phase 2 below) remains a defense-in-depth future
enhancement, not a shipped gate — the shipped model is **per-log** admission, so an
admitted peer's ops are trusted wholesale (the accepted equivocation tradeoff), which is
why the GitHub re-derivation invariant is what actually carries the safety.

**Build-state update (2026-06-25).** Read admission is intentionally **not** a
repo-collaborator permission gate. The pure decider in
`sync/hyperbee/read-admission.ts` admits a log only after announce signature
verification, GitHub-gist attestation verification, and the `revoked_pubkeys`
veto. Boot adds two Pot-specific scope wideners: an already-known Pot member
can be admitted from the local `hive_members` projection via
`trustedHiveMemberDeviceAdmission`, and a same-Pot cross-member announce whose
membership has not federated yet is buffered as `pending` and retried within the
boot grace window. GitHub collaborator/admin permission remains the authority
for repo binding, revocation actions, push/PR/merge, and shipped verification;
it is not the swarm read-admission allow-list.
</Aside>

<Aside type="note" title="Build-state update (A-003 / a′) — slug-aware admission scope">
When one hive topic carries **multiple local harnesses'** log announces (a joiner's member
harness sharing the same topic as the hive-home log it rebinds from), the D-004 identity
decider alone would let any identity-valid frame be admitted by **every** on-topic handler —
since every harness registers all projections, a wrong-scope log could then cross-merge (e.g.
the owner's hive-home harness applying a member-log's features into the hive-home schema).
`announceSlugInScope` (`read-admission.ts`) is a pure, no-I/O predicate applied **after** the
D-004 identity decision (`boot.ts`'s `onAnnounce`): it admits an inbound log only if its
**signed** origin-slug is either this harness's own slug, or the hive-home slug it rebinds
(`joinerPotHomeSlug`). An absent origin-slug (legacy/single-harness peers, pre-dating the field)
is admitted for backward compatibility. A scope miss returns `out_of_scope` — conclusive, never
retried, distinct from the identity decider's own `bad_sig`/`binding_invalid`/`revoked`/`pending`.
</Aside>

## What a shared harness is

A shared harness lets several engineers collaborate on one coding project. Shared state —
the **feature queue, pull-request status, the contributor list, and feature "claims"** —
syncs peer-to-peer over the Holepunch stack and is projected into each peer's local
Postgres:

- **Hyperswarm** — DHT peer discovery. The swarm **topic = `sha256("papercusp-substrate-v1:gh:<github_repository_id>")`**, derived from the *public* GitHub repo id, so it is **discoverable, not a secret**. `gh:<repository_id>` is only one of several topic bindings: the shipped multi-engineer (**Pot**) substrate is keyed by **`pot:<hive_pubkey>`**, which *replaces* the per-repo slug as the top-level federation unit (a Pot's Swarms all join this one topic), with `local:<workspace_id>/<slug>` for pre-binding/private dev and an explicit `topic:<hex>` carrier so a link-joiner lands on the owner's exact Pot topic rather than re-deriving a `gh:` topic that wouldn't match.
- **Hypercore** — one Ed25519-signed append-only log per device.
- **Model B peer-log** — one single-writer Ed25519 log per device + a read-merge over the others (`sync/hyperbee/peer-log.ts`). This **replaced** the earlier multi-writer **Autobase** design; Autobase mentions below are the historical survey/analysis, not the shipped substrate (P-024 truth fix).

Identity is anchored to **GitHub**: each device holds an Ed25519 keypair in the OS
keychain. The OAuth `GET /user` channel is a **local self-attestation only — it is never
part of remote admission**. Remote admission (post write-free-join) proves the
`device_pubkey ↔ github_user_id` binding entirely from a **device-signed announce** plus
`verifyAttestation` on a **public GitHub gist** — the gist pins `owner.id ===
github_user_id`, the body's `device_pubkey`, and a device signature. There is **no
device-signed commit** anywhere in the code: the old shared-repo contributor-file channel
was removed in the write-free-join work.

The single most important fact: **the authority for the one thing that truly matters —
merging code — is GitHub itself.** PRs merge through the GitHub REST API with a real user
token, so GitHub's write-access and branch-protection rules are enforced regardless of
anything that happens on the swarm.

## The trust problem

<Aside type="danger" title="Original 2026-05-31 state: the substrate was wide open">
Replicated Autobase ops were **not signed, authenticated, or authorized on receipt** — the
only admission check was a schema-version filter. Because the swarm topic is derivable from
the public repo id, **any peer who could reach the DHT could join and write forged
feature/PR/contributor/claim rows into every other peer's local database.** The designed
defenses (an admission step gated on the two-channel binding, a `revoked_pubkeys`
drop-list) existed on paper but had **no production callers**.

**Update (2026-06-13):** admission is now wired (Model B per-log: signed announce +
GitHub-anchored `verifyBinding` + `revoked_pubkeys` veto — see
`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/read-admission.ts`), so a peer is admitted only
on a verified GitHub-anchored attestation, not by mere DHT reachability. What remains
**intentionally** unbuilt is **per-op** signature verification at projection time: once a
peer is admitted, its ops are projected wholesale (the accepted equivocation tradeoff). The
forged-advisory-row surface is therefore narrowed to *already-admitted* peers and, per the
verified invariant below, **no decision-bearing action acts on those rows without
re-deriving from GitHub**.
</Aside>

Keep two threat models separate:

- **Untrustworthy local user** — every local API route is `auth: 'public'` (127.0.0.1
  only). It trusts whoever is on the desktop. Fine for a single-user desktop; not a
  shared-machine model.
- **Untrustworthy swarm peer** *(the serious one)* — public topic + unsigned ops means a
  peer can poison every other peer's local DB/UI. This is what the security layer exists to
  contain.

A code audit (2026-05-31) confirmed that **GitHub is the only authorization actually
enforced today.** Everything Papercusp layers on top — the feature state machine, the PR
"trusted authors" gate, the `completion_ref` "shipped ✓" verifier, contributor identity
signatures, and substrate op-auth — is currently dead code, unwired, or self-asserted.

## How other systems solve it

A three-pass survey of production P2P / local-first / decentralized systems. They converge
on a small primitive set: **sign every replicated write and verify it on receipt; gate
membership cryptographically; anchor identity to keys or an external authority; and accept
that true deletion is impossible in an append-only log.**

| System | Identity anchor | Per-op authorization | Membership / removal | Verdict for Papercusp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hypercore** | per-device Ed25519 key (our model) | signed merkle tree per log (integrity, single-writer) | — | **Maps** — proves you authored *your* log, not that you're allowed |
| **Autobase** | — | **none built in**; *"optimistic blocks should self-verify in the apply handler"* | `addWriter`/`removeWriter` are app calls inside `apply` | **Maps / confirms the gap** — per-op verification is the app's job |
| **Hyperswarm / HyperDHT** | connecting peer's Noise key | Noise authenticates the *connection*, not ops | only `firewall(remotePublicKey)` | **Maps / confirms threat** — public topic; connection-auth ≠ op-auth |
| **blind-pairing** (Keet) | invite secret | candidate signs with invite key; member verifies | admit-by-invite; app-evaluated `userData` | **Partial** — a ready admission handshake; put the GitHub proof in `userData` |
| **Radicle** *(closest analog)* | self-sovereign `did:key` (opposite of ours) | **signs every write** (`refs/rad/sigref`); **rejects invalid before storing**; signed collaborative objects | delegate threshold/quorum | **Mechanism maps, anchor doesn't** — proves the sign-and-verify-before-store pattern |
| **Radicle COBs** | content-addressed | exposes each change's author → filter a bad author at view-build | filter at materialization | **Maps** — our `revoked_pubkeys` is this *local projection filter*, not network rejection |
| **Kleppmann (BFT-CRDT)** | — | **signatures necessary but NOT sufficient** — a signed *equivocation* breaks version vectors | a replicated ACL must itself be a BFT CRDT | **Decisive** — don't try to make advisory state Byzantine-trustworthy |
| **Keyhive / BeeKEM** (Ink & Switch) | **deliberately excludes** identity binding | capability chains + per-op Ed25519 sig; BeeKEM needs only **causal** order → fits Autobase | coordination-free removal with **real post-compromise security** | **Authz maps; complements (≠ replaces) the GitHub binding** — see [Keyhive](#does-keyhivebeekem-fit-our-stack) |
| **MLS / RFC 9420** | — | TreeKEM epoch chain | needs **one linear chain of agreed Commits**; concurrent commits fork a DAG it can't merge | **Does not map** over Autobase's concurrent merge |
| **Keybase** *(two-channel analog)* | per-user signed **sigchain**; key↔GitHub via a GitHub-hosted signed proof | each link signed, `seqno` + `prev` hash | revocation = a **signed revoke link**; sibkeys for device-loss recovery | **Maps — improves the binding**: model two-channel as a signed link; revoke-as-signed-statement beats a side-list |
| **Sigstore / SLSA / in-toto** | short-lived **OIDC** identity (Fulcio) | keyless sig + **Rekor transparency log**; in-toto/DSSE | no revocation (short-lived certs); compromise caught by **monitoring** | **Partial — provenance pattern**: a signature proves *authenticated-at-a-time*, **not** authorization or "good." Confirms "shipped" must be **GitHub-derived** |
| **AT Proto `did:plc`** | hybrid: self-cert keys + a directory | signed repo commits | **rotation-key priority list + 72h recovery window** | **Partial — recovery lesson**: for us, GitHub *is* the recovery anchor |
| **Nostr NIP-05** | pubkey ↔ `name@domain` via a `.well-known` file | per-event Schnorr sig | — | **Partial** — a GitHub-hosted well-known file is a lighter binding variant |
| **Secure Scuttlebutt** | per-identity signed append-only feed (≈ Hypercore) | every message signed | **invite + follow-graph** bounds replication & Sybils | **Partial — admission analog**: Pot membership + revocation bounds shared-pot replication; GitHub permission is reserved for decision-bearing actions |

### The decisive constraints

1. **Autobase will not authenticate ops for us** — per-op signing and `addWriter` gating
   are *our* code, in the `apply`/projection seam.
2. **Signatures are necessary but not sufficient** (Kleppmann) — a validly-admitted-then-
   malicious writer can sign false or *equivocating* rows. Full Byzantine resilience needs
   a hash-DAG causal layer we are **not** going to build.
3. **True removal / post-compromise security is impossible in an append-only multi-writer
   log** — a revoked writer's signed ops persist and replicate; "removal" means every
   honest peer drops them at projection time.
4. **A provenance signature proves authentication-at-a-time, not authorization or quality**
   (Sigstore) — so the trustworthy "shipped" signal must come from GitHub's *merge state*,
   not a self-reported receipt.
5. **GitHub already enforces the only hard authorization that matters.** This is the escape
   hatch from the unsolved Byzantine-CRDT access-control problem.

## Does Holepunch provide its own solution?

Mostly the **building blocks**, not a turnkey access-control product:

- **Hypercore** signs each log for free.
- **Autobase** gives a writer set with `addWriter`/`removeWriter`, but **you** write the
  per-op check and the admission policy in `apply`.
- **blind-pairing-core** (what Keet actually uses) is a real cryptographic invite/pairing
  handshake — admit-by-possession-of-invite-secret. This is Holepunch's native admission
  answer.
- **Hyperswarm** gives Noise-encrypted connections + a coarse `firewall(remotePublicKey)`
  reject hook.

What Holepunch deliberately leaves to the app: fine-grained capabilities (read/write/admin),
**identity binding** (always app-layer — our GitHub anchor), and **post-compromise security
on removal** (`removeWriter` stops new appends; it is not key-rotation/PCS). Of those, the
only one we actually need is identity binding — which no library provides.

**So the plan builds on Holepunch's native primitives**: per-op signature verification +
GitHub-anchored `addWriter` (via blind-pairing, GitHub proof in `userData`) + a
`revoked_pubkeys` projection drop-list.

## Does Keyhive/BeeKEM fit our stack?

Compatible *in principle*, but **not native and arguably overkill**:

- **It fits the ordering model** — BeeKEM needs only a *causal* order, which Autobase
  provides. It's the only post-compromise-secure option that works over a concurrent-merge
  log (MLS does not).
- **But it's an Automerge-ecosystem Rust library** (the `beekem` crate), not a Holepunch
  component. Adopting it means embedding that crate and running its control ops over
  Autobase — an unsupported combination, and it is **pre-alpha, unaudited, BeeKEM not
  formally proven**.
- **It couples authorization with *encryption*** (it's a continuous group key agreement).
  Our substrate data is plaintext to swarm members today; BeeKEM means encrypting group
  state with key rotation — a large shift that *buys* post-compromise security but is more
  than advisory data needs.
- **It still doesn't solve identity** — Keyhive defers human-identity binding to "a future
  layer above," i.e. our GitHub anchor regardless.

<Aside type="note" title="Verdict on Keyhive">
For the recommended model (advisory peer state re-derived from GitHub) we **do not need
Keyhive**. Holepunch's native primitives + the GitHub anchor are sufficient. Keyhive/BeeKEM
is a deferred upgrade **only if** a concrete requirement emerges for state that must be
*confidential to members and survive a key compromise without GitHub*.
</Aside>

## Recommended model — GitHub is the authority of record

1. **Authority of record = GitHub.** Every *decision-bearing* fact (did it merge, who has
   write access, real PR status, who is a contributor) is **re-derived from GitHub at the
   point of action** — never trusted from a peer.
2. **Peer-synced rows = advisory cache** (fast/offline UI), explicitly untrusted.
3. **Per-op Ed25519 signing + verify-on-receipt** in the Autobase `apply`/projection path —
   *defense-in-depth / UX integrity*, not the authority of record. **Sign sequence +
   freshness, not just content** (Radicle's 2026 replay-CVE lesson).
4. **GitHub-anchored log admission** — signed announce + GitHub gist attestation
   verifies the device identity; `revoked_pubkeys` denies known-bad devices. Pot
   scope is then narrowed/widened by signed `harness_slug`, local `hive_members`,
   and pending retry for membership propagation. This is not a collaborator
   permission gate.
5. **Identity binding = a Keybase-style signed link** — the GitHub-hosted device-signed
   proof is the cross-check that lets any peer detect a rewritten identity; revocation is a
   *signed* statement, not just a side list.
6. **Device-key rotation/recovery is GitHub-rooted** — losing a device means re-running the
   two-channel binding from the new device; the old key goes on `revoked_pubkeys`. GitHub
   (the account) plays `did:plc`'s "higher-authority key" recovery role.
7. **"Shipped"/provenance = GitHub-derived** — read merge state from GitHub; optionally
   record it as a signed in-toto-style attestation. Do **not** build a Rekor-style
   transparency log — GitHub already is the authority and stores attestations. (This also
   means the `completion_ref` "shipped" signal should be GitHub-derived, not a self-reported
   peer receipt.)
8. **Sybil/admission = verified GitHub identity plus Pot membership/revocation.**
   The swarm topic is public, so unauthenticated devices are filtered by signed
   announce + gist attestation; shared-Pot cross-member scope is filtered by
   `hive_members`; and `revoked_pubkeys` is the hard local blocklist. The GitHub
   collaborator graph is still consulted at decision points that need repo
   authority, but it is not the read-admission allow-list.
9. **Do not** adopt MLS or build a Byzantine-CRDT ACL.

### The advisory-vs-trusted boundary

The central decision: which synced surfaces are advisory vs must-re-derive-from-GitHub.

| Synced surface | Advisory (peer-supplied cache)? | Decision-bearing → re-derive from GitHub? |
|---|---|---|
| Feature queue / status | yes — display & coordination | a "shipped" decision → GitHub merge state |
| PR status | yes — display | merge / approval authority → GitHub |
| Contributor list | yes — display | "is X a real contributor / has write access" → GitHub collaborators |
| Feature claims | yes — coordination/UX only | (advisory by nature; no hard authority needed) |
| Completion / "shipped ✓" | no | **GitHub-derived only** |

Anything in the right column must never be acted on from peer state alone.

### Confirmation pass — 2026-06-13 (P-017): every decision-bearing fact re-derives

The shipped substrate uses **per-log** admission: a peer is admitted on a verified
signed-announce + GitHub-anchored attestation, after which its ops are trusted **wholesale**
into the projection (no per-op authz — the accepted equivocation tradeoff). That is safe
**iff** every decision-bearing fact re-derives from GitHub at the point of action. A
call-site audit (plan `shared-pot-hardening-2026-06-13`, P-017) confirmed this invariant
holds across **all** authorization-bearing consumers of peer-synced state — there is **no
gap**. The federated tables are `contributors`, `queue` / `features-by-id`
(→ `harness_features_consolidated`), `working-set`/`claims`, `presence`, plans, and
coord; the table below enumerates every site that *acts* on one (display-only reads omitted).
PR state is **not** federated: `harness_feature_prs` was reclassified `sync:'none'`
(EI-479) — it is GitHub-derived and re-polled per-machine, so Postgres is the local
store-of-record and federation is redundant; it has no projection producer and is not a
registered projection tag. (This is why the auto-merge row below correctly reads the `Pr`
object from a live GitHub poll, not from a federated row.)

| Call-site | Authorization decision | Reads | Re-derives from GitHub? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harness/binding-service.ts` · `claimBinding` | claim a repo binding (needs maintain/admin) | local cache + **live** `getRepoPermission` | **Yes** — `getRepoPermission(owner,repo,login)` at point of action |
| `harness/binding-service.ts` · `supersedeBinding` | supersede a binding (needs admin) | local cache + **live** `getRepoPermission` | **Yes** — live permission check, admin required |
| `harness/binding-service.ts` · claimant re-verify sweep | demote a claimant who lost write access | cached claimants | **Yes** — per-claimant live permission check |
| `sync/hyperbee/revoke-contributor.ts` | revoke a contributor's device key | `contributors` row | **Yes** — `repos.get → permissions.admin` gate before any write |
| `sync/hyperbee/read-admission.ts` (+ `boot.ts`) | admit a peer's log to the substrate | signed announce + local Pot membership projection | **Yes** — announce-sig verify + `verifyBinding` (GitHub-hosted attestation); `revoked_pubkeys` veto; same-Pot scope uses `hive_members` / pending retry, not repo collaborator permission |
| `harness/fork-pr-on-feature-pass.ts` | fork-PR vs direct-push mode on feature pass | local pipeline pass event | **Yes** — **live** `getPermission` (fork iff `read`/`none`) |
| `pr-host/auto-merge.ts` · `tryAutoMerge` → `host.merge` | merge a PR | `Pr` object from **GitHub** poll (`PrHost`/`github.ts`) | **Yes** — PR state read live from GitHub; merge enforced by GitHub write-access + branch protection |
| `pr-host/auto-approve.ts` · `tryAutoApprove` | post an approving review | **local** `trusted_authors` + GitHub PR author | **N/A** — trust list is local config (not federated); approval still doesn't bypass GitHub's merge authority |
| `harness/completion-ref-verifier.ts` | stamp the "shipped ✓" verified tier | `completion_ref` on the feature row | **Yes** — `git ls-remote <remote> <sha>` (GitHub native auth) confirms the SHA is on the remote |
| `dbos/orchestrator-finalize.ts` · `reconcileDoneStatus` | flip a feature `validating`/`in_progress → passed` | `harness_features_consolidated.status` (federated) | **N/A — advisory.** Fires only from the **local** orchestrator's own pipeline reaching an unblocked DONE (`outcome==='done'`); a peer's forged row cannot make the local pipeline run a feature to DONE. `passed` is internal pipeline coordination, **not** a "shipped"/authz fact — every downstream effect (push/PR/merge) is independently GitHub-gated. (Completion-integrity update, `fleet-backlog-lessons-2026-07-01` P-001/WI-1542: the same local-only write now also stamps `terminal_owner='system:dbos-orchestrator-finalize'` and a `terminal_completion_ref` — an auditability fix for the genuine-completions metric, not a change to who may write or to the trust boundary.) |
| `contributors` / `claims` / `queue` / `working-set` readers (claim avatars, status badges, queue UI) | display & coordination only | federated rows | **N/A** — advisory by design; gate no action |

**Why the federated feature `status` is not a gap (the one row worth tracing).**
`harness_features_consolidated.status` *is* a federated projection target (tag
`features-by-id`), so an admitted peer can write a `status` value into another peer's PG.
But no authorization decision acts on it: a forged `status='shipped'` does not earn the
verified ✓ badge (that re-derives via `git ls-remote`), and `reconcileDoneStatus` only
closes the `validating`/`in_progress`→`passed` loop (the `in_progress` case was added
2026-06-17 for coding-harness cups that skip the validator step) as the **local** pipeline's
own terminal verdict on a feature it actually executed — it cannot be driven by a
peer-supplied row; terminal-failure states (failing/deprecated) are left untouched. The real "did it
ship" authority remains GitHub's merge state, and code only lands through GitHub's
write-access + branch-protection. This is the security doc's own placement of "feature
queue / status" in the **advisory** column, confirmed at the code level.

**Verdict:** the wholesale-trust-of-admitted-peer model is sound **because** the
re-derivation invariant is universal. No remediation needed; P-017 closed `done`.

### Revocation chokepoints (built)

Two revocation mechanisms are wired beyond the `revoked_pubkeys` admission drop-list:

- **PR auto-approve and auto-merge refuse a revoked contributor's PR up front.** A PR whose
  author is a revoked Pot contributor is denied (action `skipped_revoked`) **before** the
  trust / checks / approval gates — the strongest deny, **overriding the trust list** (it
  holds even for an author otherwise in `trusted_authors`). The live chokepoint resolves it
  via `isHiveContributorRevoked` and passes it into both `tryAutoApprove` and `tryAutoMerge`.
- **Owner-revocation of another contributor** (`revokeContributorViaGithub`) is gated on a
  **live GitHub repo-admin** check (`repos.get → permissions.admin`) — the harness-owner
  authority. It works by unioning the target's device pubkeys into the **owner's own**
  contributor-row `revoked_pubkeys` and publishing it (the old "delete the `user/<id>`
  branch" lever became a no-op under write-free join, and an admin cannot delete another
  user's attestation gist). Because `load-revoked-pubkeys` **unions `revoked_pubkeys` across
  all contributor rows** for the harness, that block federates via the owner's log and is
  honored by every peer's admission union.

## Accepted-insecurity tradeoffs

Under this model we **deliberately accept**:

1. **Public, discoverable topic** — swarm spam/DoS is *mitigated* (firewall + admission),
   not prevented.
2. **Advisory rows can be injected by an admitted identity** — read admission proves
   identity and Pot membership, not truth. An admitted-then-malicious writer can
   still inject signed-but-false advisory rows (equivocation). Mitigation:
   nothing decision-bearing acts on it without GitHub re-derivation.
3. **No true removal / no post-compromise security** in the append-only log — revocation is
   best-effort projection filtering; the data persists and replicates.
4. **Sybil resistance is mostly delegated to GitHub identity plus Pot membership** —
   identity = GitHub account, bounded by the gist attestation and GitHub's
   account-creation friction; cross-member shared-Pot writes also require a
   current `hive_members` device row or they remain pending/dropped.
5. **Per-op signatures don't defeat a signed equivocator** (Kleppmann) — accepted because
   state is advisory and GitHub-re-derived; we explicitly do not build a BFT-CRDT ACL.
6. **Identity binding inherits GitHub account integrity** — a compromised GitHub account is
   a compromised identity (the same trust root as the merge authority, so not a new
   exposure).
7. **Local API stays loopback-trusted** — a single-user-desktop model, not a shared machine.

## Phased implementation

- **Phase 1 — make peer state advisory + re-derive from GitHub.** Highest value, lowest
  risk; neutralizes the forgery surface for anything that matters. Resolves `completion_ref`
  as a GitHub-derived "shipped" signal.
- **Phase 2 — per-op Ed25519 signing + verify-on-receipt** in the `apply`/projection path
  (sign seq + content); drop unverifiable ops at projection.
- **Phase 3 — GitHub-anchored `addWriter` admission** (two-channel proof in blind-pairing
  `userData`) + `revoked_pubkeys` projection drop-list; model the binding as a signed link.
- **Phase 4 — only if a threat model demands real PCS** — Keyhive/BeeKEM membership.

## Sources & method

Three deep-research passes (web search → fetch primary sources → adversarial verification),
~9M tokens. Passes 1–2 (50 claims verified): Holepunch repos, Radicle (Heartwood +
`radicle-cob` + LWN), ForgeFed, Kleppmann (PaPoC'22 + keynote), Ink & Switch Keyhive
notebook, RFC 9420/9750 + DMLS drafts. Pass 3 (Keybase, Sigstore/SLSA, `did:plc`, Nostr,
SSB): primary-sourced but the workflow's vote-tally step crashed, so those rows are
extracted-not-triple-verified; the two most decision-relevant (Sigstore threat model,
`did:plc` recovery) were re-confirmed by direct fetch. Full per-claim detail lives in the
design memo `apps/operator/docs/plans/papercusp-trust-model-2026-05-31.md`.
